chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Nightclub work then vaudeville in New York, never in a pit
summary: Kuehl tries to pin down the order of his early work; Basie says Feather's statement is true but misplaced as a debut.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Okay, well, okay. So, I guess then, somehow, sometime between leaving, taking your lessons from Grace [Mowchow] and so forth, then you were gigging by yourself in New Jersey or a combination or were you out on your own, you know, playing? I guess you don't hear the questions.
All right, from -- so anyway, we do know that that's not true. You weren't doing theater work --
I mean, it did -- it is true, but he's just got it placed (inaudible) --

Okay. Okay. All right, could we say then chronologically that you were playing for nightclub acts in New York? Without being specific, you were playing for nightclub acts in New York and then played vaudeville in New York before you left New York? I mean, would that be true?
Let me ask you a question.
If you were me, and you were being asked that question, would you really give it?
In what sense do you mean?
In the sense you asked it.
I mean, I'd say sure, it's true or no, it's not true.
Well, that isn't the question you asked me.
I asked you, is it true that you first played nightclubs in New York and before leaving New York, you were then playing in the pit. That's what I mean. That's what my question was.
I never played in a pit,
I guess maybe he might have thought that I played for (inaudible).
Okay. I say -- you mean, if he thought vaudeville acts were singers, you mean, in that sense, he could have been --
Then it would be true. Okay, I see.
Well, maybe he meant later years, too, maybe he's speaking about later years, when I came to New York with my band.
No, he's saying the first time you ever played professionally.
